competitions.result: Fourth round — lost 1–0 away to Arsenal.
Third round — lost 2–1 at home to Grimsby Town.
Champions League quarter-final — lost 4–3 on aggregate to Bayer Leverkusen.

out.note: Returned at the end of his loan in May 2002.

overview: Liverpool finished second in the Premier League with 80 points, seven behind Arsenal. They added the Charity Shield and UEFA Super Cup in August, beating Manchester United 2–1 and Bayern Munich 3–2 respectively. These were the fourth and fifth trophies won during calendar year 2001.

Gérard Houllier fell ill during the home match against Leeds on 13 October and underwent heart surgery. Phil Thompson took temporary charge during his recovery. Houllier returned to the dugout for the 2–0 win over Roma on 19 March, which secured a Champions League quarter-final place. Bayer Leverkusen then eliminated Liverpool 4–3 on aggregate.

Michael Owen scored 28 competitive goals and received the European Footballer of the Year award during the season. John Arne Riise and Jerzy Dudek joined, while Robbie Fowler moved to Leeds and Nicolas Anelka arrived on loan from Paris Saint-Germain. Arsenal ended Liverpool’s FA Cup defence in the fourth round; Grimsby Town had already knocked them out of the League Cup.
